messages:
Carlos: Hi team, since ~10:42 UTC our production app started seeing spikes in generation latency and occasional 503s. Customers report token streaming stops mid-response. Request IDs: req_0a1b2c3d, req_0f9e8d7c. Also saw some 401s when refreshing tokens around the same time. Any known rollouts?
Maya: sorry you're hitting this! can you paste one of the failing request IDs and a curl you used? can you also confirm if customer is pinning model/version in the request?
Carlos: putting a quick curl we used (sanitized):
```
curl -i https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gptx-3.8","input":"Summarize...","pin":"canary-2024-10"}'
```
Response headers: `x-request-id: req_0a1b2c3d`, status `503` or sometimes `200` but stream stalls after ~120 tokens.
Maya: thanks — that pin looks like a canary variant. tagging infra. @Jonah can you check canary pool health and fallback rules?
Jonah: saw an automated canary swap around 10:40 UTC. ops-bot logged a partial rollback attempt at 10:41 but it looks like fallback paths were misaligned for pinned requests. grabbing traces for req_0a1b2c3d / req_0f9e8d7c.
ops-bot: deploy-job: canary rollout for model gptx-3.8 -> canary-2024-10 started at 2025-02-14T10:40:12Z. partial rollback initiated at 2025-02-14T10:41:05Z.
Priya: possibility: pinned requests bypass routing that would normally fallback to stable. if the canary instance had a KV cache mismatch or different kernel set, streaming can stall. please collect debug bundle and full server logs for those request ids (runtime + proxy).
Carlos: I'm prepping logs now. are there minimal repro steps you want?
Maya: yes — two quick repros we need: 1) reproduce with model pin to confirm canary behavior, 2) reproduce without pin to see stable fallback. For each, include a curl with `-H "X-Debug: true"` to force trace headers, and capture `x-request-id` and `x-trace-id`. Example:
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Debug: true" \
  -d '{"model":"gptx-3.8","input":"test","pin":"canary-2024-10"}'
```
Also please attach the proxy logs around the request timestamps and the auth token payload (no secrets) if you can.
Carlos: uploaded `support-debug-1850004321.tar.gz` to the secure bucket (link sent to support inbox). included proxy logs and app logs.
Jonah: pulling the bundle now. quick heads-up: I can see 401 spikes for a different client token earlier at 10:39 — looks like a separate token refresh race, but I don't think that's causing the 503 streaming stalls.
Priya: got the traces for req_0a1b2c3d. runtime shows streaming blocked waiting on a KV cache load on canary nodes, then a kernel fallback that timed out after 30s. that's consistent with resource mismatch on canary.
Maya: thanks. next steps: we should gather a minimal curl repro (pin vs unpinned) from Carlos so we can run it against canary and stable pools in staging. Also we'll need to consider a temporary pin override for this customer to stable and initiate a full rollback for canary.
ops-bot: maintenance: rolling back canary-2024-10 -> stable at 2025-02-14T10:55:00Z (initiated by Jonah). ETA ~4m.
Carlos: can you pin me to stable while you investigate? urgent customer SLA.
Jonah: will do. applying a temporary pin override for customer-id 98765 to `gptx-3.8@stable` now.
Priya: I'll open an internal postmortem ticket and capture regressions in the canary config (KV serialization + kernel packing). tagging runtime and oncall.
Maya: I have everything I need to escalate billing/auth separately if it resurfaces. for now focus on repro + rollback. I'll update the customer and ask them to run the two curl variants with `X-Debug: true` and attach new request-ids here. :thumbsup:
Carlos: thanks all — running the two quick curl tests now, will paste new req ids in a sec.
